accuracy_policy: skip_unverified_keys; correct_index=-1 if answer not certain

questions.subject: BIOLOGY
questions.prompt: Morphology is the branch of biology concerned with:
explanation_steps: Morphology is the study of the form and structure of organisms.
questions.correct_answer_text: the general form of organisms.

questions.subject: BIOLOGY
questions.prompt: A control experiment:
options: is a repeat of the original experiment to make sure the results are reproducible.
is carried out at a constant temperature.
is always carried out under the controlled conditions of a laboratory.
helps to interpret the results of the main experiment.
is simpler than a real experiment.
explanation_steps: A control provides a baseline so the effect of the independent variable can be interpreted.
questions.correct_answer_text: helps to interpret the results of the main experiment.

questions.subject: BIOLOGY
questions.prompt: Adaptation is the process by which:
options: new varieties of plants are selected for use in agriculture.
organisms become better suited to their environment.
individuals of one species interact with individuals of another species.
a reflex reaction occurs in response to an unusual stimulus.
non-biological parents care for a child.
explanation_steps: Adaptation is becoming better suited to environmental conditions.
questions.correct_answer_text: organisms become better suited to their environment.

questions.subject: BIOLOGY
questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is not true of cell theory?
options: The cell is the structural unit of life.
The cell is the unit of function of living things.
The molecules of life are the products of cellular activity.
Cells are surrounded by a cell wall.
explanation_steps: Cell wall is not part of cell theory; animal cells lack walls.
questions.correct_answer_text: Cells are surrounded by a cell wall.

questions.subject: BIOLOGY
questions.prompt: According to the modern classification of organisms, humans are members of:
explanation_steps: Humans belong to phylum Chordata. Other options use the wrong rank.
questions.correct_answer_text: the chordate phylum.

questions.subject: BIOLOGY
questions.prompt: Algae:
options: occur in most permanent or semi-permanent bodies of water.
have specialised tissues for conducting water and food.
explanation_steps: Most algae are aquatic autotrophs without true vascular tissue.
questions.correct_answer_text: occur in most permanent or semi-permanent bodies of water.

questions.subject: BIOLOGY
questions.prompt: Yeasts:
options: refer to several kinds of fungi that form mycelium.
are major parasites of crop plants, particularly the cereals.
are used in the process of industrial fermentation.
explanation_steps: Yeasts are unicellular fungi used in industrial fermentation.
questions.correct_answer_text: are used in the process of industrial fermentation.

questions.subject: BIOLOGY
questions.prompt: Bryophytes differ from pterophytes in that bryophytes:
options: lack specialised tissues for conducting water and food.
explanation_steps: Bryophytes are non-vascular; ferns have vascular tissue.
questions.correct_answer_text: lack specialised tissues for conducting water and food.

questions.subject: BIOLOGY
questions.prompt: Monocots and dicots are the same in their:
explanation_steps: Both are seed-producing angiosperms.
questions.correct_answer_text: capacity to produce seeds.

questions.subject: BIOLOGY
questions.prompt: An example of nastic movement in plants is:
options: roots grow down, while shoots grow up.
the closing of a flower in the evening.
root growth towards water or nutrients.
explanation_steps: Nastic movements are non-directional; tropisms are directional growth.
questions.correct_answer_text: the closing of a flower in the evening.

questions.subject: BIOLOGY
questions.prompt: Transpiration refers to:
options: the transportation of water from roots to leaves.
the evaporation of water from above-ground parts of a plant.
the exchange of gases that takes place at the surface of a leaf.
the absorption of water through non-root parts of the plant.
the transport of nutrients through the vascular system of a plant.
explanation_steps: Transpiration is evaporative water loss from aerial parts.
questions.correct_answer_text: the evaporation of water from above-ground parts of a plant.

questions.subject: BIOLOGY
questions.prompt: Mitosis ensures that:
options: children are genetically different from their parents.
each new body cell has the same genetic make-up as its parent cell.
gametes are produced for the next generation.
explanation_steps: Mitosis yields genetically identical body cells.
questions.correct_answer_text: each new body cell has the same genetic make-up as its parent cell.

questions.subject: BIOLOGY
questions.prompt: In the second division of meiosis:
explanation_steps: Meiosis II separates sister chromatids.
questions.correct_answer_text: chromatids separate.

questions.subject: BIOLOGY
questions.prompt: In parthenogenesis:
options: two parents are required to produce each offspring.
the offspring are genetically different from the parents.
an unfertilised egg develops into an embryo.
a single-celled organism divides into two equal daughter cells.
explanation_steps: Parthenogenesis is development from an unfertilised egg.
questions.correct_answer_text: an unfertilised egg develops into an embryo.

questions.subject: BIOLOGY
questions.prompt: In one of Mendel's crosses, all self-pollinated F1 plants were green. In the F2 generation, Mendel counted 428 green plants and 152 yellow plants. These results can be explained by:
explanation_steps: 3:1 ratio is segregation; F1 all green is dominance.
questions.correct_answer_text: B and C.

questions.subject: BIOLOGY
questions.prompt: In the fruit fly, gray body is dominant over black body. Two gray flies were mated to produce 158 gray and 49 black offspring. Both gray parents must have been:
explanation_steps: 3:1 and recessive offspring require both parents heterozygous.
questions.correct_answer_text: heterozygous.

questions.subject: BIOLOGY
questions.prompt: The power of selection in modifying populations over time can be demonstrated by:
options: field observations and experiments in natural environments.
the response of bacteria to antibiotics.
explanation_steps: Lab, field, pigeon breeding and antibiotic resistance all show selection.
questions.correct_answer_text: all of the above.

questions.subject: BIOLOGY
questions.prompt: An example of a structure which is not vestigial is:
options: the eyes of a fish that lives in a cave where there is no sunlight.
the muscles that move human ears.
explanation_steps: Mitochondria are essential organelles, not vestigial organs.
questions.correct_answer_text: the human mitochondria.

questions.subject: BIOLOGY
questions.prompt: In ecological studies, a community refers to:
options: a group of individuals within a species living in a particular place at the same time.
the complex of interactions between living and non-living parts of the environment.
a group of families within a species living in a particular place at the same time.
an extended family which depends upon one another for food and shelter.
populations of organisms that live together in a specific area and depend upon one another for food and shelter.
explanation_steps: A community is interacting populations; an ecosystem includes abiotic factors.
questions.correct_answer_text: populations of organisms that live together in a specific area and depend upon one another for food and shelter.

questions.subject: BIOLOGY
questions.prompt: What would happen if a person's bile duct became blocked?
options: The duodenum contents would be neutralised more quickly.
explanation_steps: Bile emulsifies fats; blockage reduces fat digestion.
questions.correct_answer_text: Fat digestion would be reduced.

questions.subject: BIOLOGY
questions.prompt: Which of these metabolic processes is not a function of the liver?
explanation_steps: Conversion of fat to glycogen is not a standard liver function.
questions.correct_answer_text: Conversion of fat to glycogen

questions.subject: BIOLOGY
questions.prompt: Nucleases are enzymes which can break down ____ into their smaller units:
explanation_steps: Nucleases hydrolyse nucleic acids.
questions.correct_answer_text: DNA or RNA.

questions.subject: BIOLOGY
questions.prompt: The main function of the finger like projections known as villi on the wall of the small intestine is:
options: to promote food absorption by increasing the surface area of the small intestine.
to promote food absorption by decreasing the surface area of the small intestine.
explanation_steps: Villi increase absorptive surface area.
questions.correct_answer_text: to promote food absorption by increasing the surface area of the small intestine.

questions.subject: BIOLOGY
questions.prompt: The formation of blood clotting is due to the change of:
explanation_steps: Thrombin converts fibrinogen to fibrin.
questions.correct_answer_text: fibrinogen to fibrin.
